attempts.raw_response: Then, fold the fabric over about 1/4 inch with the wrong side facing out, and fold it again so the raw edge is tucked underneath. The folded edge should hang about 1 inch below your fabric. Press this fold with an iron to create a crisp line. Next, position the fabric under the blind hem foot so the folded edge sits against the guide on the foot. Lower the presser foot and select the blind hem stitch on your machine. Begin sewing slowly, allowing the zigzag part of the stitch to catch only the tiniest bit of the main fabric. When finished, press the hem flat with an iron to reveal your nearly invisible hemline.

pair.human_continuation: There are two ways to sew a hem: by hand or with a sewing machine. While the latter is obviously faster, the former allows you to sew a hem without many tools. If you can, set up your sewing machine for your hem; use a straight stitch for a double-fold hem. You’re almost done! To finish off your hem, you need to iron it so it lays down flat. If your fabric can handle it, use a bit of steam to help with the ironing process. When you’re done ironing, turn your fabric right-side-out, and enjoy your newly completed hem.
pair.prefix: In order to sew a blind hem on a sewing machine, you must have two tools: a blind hem foot, and the proper stitch. A blind hem foot can be purchased at most sewing shops for around $10. In addition, check to see if your sewing machine comes with a stitch that looks like this: ^----^----^. If you haven’t already, prewash your fabric to prevent it from shrinking later. Then, place your fabric on a countertop with the pattern side down.
